summary: Intermittent 429s on long-lived SSE sessions after HTTP/3 + per-route burst isolation enabled in private VPC
description:
Issue summary:
BrightLayer reports intermittent 429 (Too Many Requests) responses observed primarily on long-lived Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams after they migrated traffic to HTTP/3 and flipped on the new per-route burst isolation feature in their private VPC deployment. The throttles appear as short pulses (1-5s) and affect a subset of persistent clients while bulk/batch ingest remains healthy.

Impact:
- ~8% of SSE connections for a single customer region (eu-west) receive transient 429s over the 6 hour window.
- Customer reports degraded product behaviour for real-time dashboards and slow rejoin behavior.
- Customer is on a Private deployment and expects no cross-tenant quota bleed.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (VPC) deployment, control plane version: 2026.02.14
- Edge proxy: v1.12.3 (HTTP/3 enabled), per-route burst isolation flag: enabled (flipped 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC)
- Rate limiter service: v3.8.1 (epoch refill enabled, 1s granularity)
- Affected region: eu-west, only BrightLayer tenant observed

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Establish a persistent SSE subscription to /v1/streams/updates using HTTP/3 from a fleet of browser clients behind a NATed proxy.
2) Maintain 30-60 long-lived connections from a single API key (~120 concurrent per host).
3) Observe occasional 429 responses returned from edge during normal traffic; reconnect attempts see backoff and delayed rejoin.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset: small deltas (a few hundred ms), but header inconsistencies exist across multiplexed paths.
- Some connections see immediate 429 on first POST after maintenance; others run for minutes then get a short 429 pulse.
- Console shows quota readout unchanged while requests are rejected.

Expected behavior:
- Long-lived SSEs should be placed into the long-lived exemption pool or charged against an isolated burst bucket without causing tenant-wide disruption. Headers should reflect accurate remaining credits.

Logs / evidence provided by customer:
- Edge logs with timestamps, example request ids: e7b4c2a4, f9a8d3b1, 2026-03-09T02:03:11Z
- Packet traces showing QUIC connection re-establishments after 429s
- Console screenshot showing steady quota and the timing of the flip for per-route burst isolation

Initial investigation notes (Support):
- Performed spike run against a staging mirror with similar settings; observed minor refill drift when HTTP/3 connection resets were rapid and multiple paths reused the same token bucket accounting.
- Hypothesis: enabling per-route burst isolation introduced an additional accounting layer that races with ephemeral QUIC/HTTP3 connection handovers in the private edge proxy, causing short-lived double-deductions or misattributed refills to per-connection windows.
- Related config: epoch refill smoothing window set to 1s, edge keeps connection affinity for 30s; customer NAT pooling creates multipath fanout.

Workaround suggested to customer:
- Temporarily roll back per-route burst isolation flag (flip back) while we investigate (customer accepted and observed immediate reduction in 429 pulses).
- Recommend ensuring HTTP/3 QUIC connection pooling and keepalive frequency are tuned to avoid frequent handovers.

Next steps / action items:
- (SRE) Validate rate-limiter accounting under QUIC handover scenarios and reproduce double-deduct in a deterministic test harness.
- (Edge) Instrument additional debug headers for a short window to capture token-bucket assignments and route-layer attribution. PR #210 in edge-proxy adds debug traces (linked).
- (Support) Coordinate a controlled canary where we re-enable per-route flag with increased epoch smoothing (2s) and monitor.
- (Customer success) Schedule a maintenance window for a controlled test with reduced client fanout to reproduce on demand.

Status update: customer rolled flag back 2026-03-10 04:40 UTC; pulse stopped. Planning a controlled re-enable with SRE and Edge engineers on 2026-03-15.
